claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game runs poorly on the Steam Deck, specifically reporting that character movement does not work.

citations.review_text: if your on steamdeck DO NOT BUY cant move in game

This game honestly sucks.....
ON STEAM.

Broken, glitchy, stupid mess. Things flying everywhere, models glitching the hell out, goats flying into space, it's amazing and I love it so much. I can't recommend it enough....
BUT THIS PORT IS AWFUL.

It's pretty much only playable in exclusive fullscreen, so if you have more than one monitor or like switching windows often, get used to alt+tabbing. This version of the game was also never updated to include online multiplayer unlike the console versions of the game, so the only ways to play it are alone or over Steam Remote Play (which, all due respect Gabe, kinda sucks). For whatever reason, this particular version also doesn't let you switch goat mutators on the fly! If you wanna toggle something off because it's distracting you or getting in the way, you gotta go all the way back to the main menu!

So by all means, please buy this game, you won't regret it. BUT, go give your money to Microsoft, Sony or Nintendo to play it on one of their platforms instead. It's a lot better to experience there.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the physics as ridiculous and note that players can break the world, cause destruction, and get launched across the map.

citations.review_text:
Goat Simulator is the game that asks the most important question in gaming: "What if I was a goat and nobody could stop me?"

The physics are completely ridiculous, and that's exactly why the game works. You can headbutt people, launch yourself through windows, climb buildings, ragdoll across the map, and generally cause as much pointless destruction as possible.

There's no real reason to do most of the things the game lets you do — and that's the point. The fun comes from experimenting with the physics and discovering increasingly stupid ways to break the world.

The map is packed with secrets and goofy interactions, so even wandering around aimlessly can lead to something hilarious.

It isn't a serious simulator, and thankfully it never tries to be one.

10/10 — finally a realistic goat simulator where goats can summon demonic powers and destroy entire neighborhoods.
Not even 10 secs in and i somehow already got flown out of the map. 10/10

I learned that goats can:
* Fly 
* Explode
* Summon chaos
* Ignore the laws of physics

Science.

citations.review_text:
A game being bad for the sake of being bad is still a bad game. It's even worse because it seems like they actually tried.
I literally hate this game; just everything about it is so annoying and not fun to play. This is just a really stupid iPad game. I think there are better versions, but this just seems like a port. You can't even change the mutators of the goat while playing; you have to go back to the main menu. There's also some really annoying audio bugs that make the voice lines of NPCs play at maximum volume when I have the game's volume sliders all turned to zero. It certainly doesn't help when every single NPC in the immediate area begins yelling and screaming when slightly touching one of them. It's also just REALLY FUN to have your computer get basically frozen when alt+tabbing in and out of the window, which happened to me three times in one sit-down. Awesome... I really love that.
It's really a shame that this game is so bad because the concept of this game, being satire and whatnot, is actually sort of silly and fun on paper, but it's just so bad and there is so much to the game that it all just feels like junk. I really enjoyed playing this when I was much younger, but playing it now and getting all of the achievements just makes me want to vomit from how ugly and broken this game is.
Also, the controls on the spaceship in the Waste of Space map are genuinely atrocious, so bad that I thought it was a joke until I realized that there are achievements associated with it.

"Too Many Goats" - 1/10 IGN

Wait nvm there's an achievement where you need to make the human centipede out of goats - 10/10 Brazzers

The real review:
A Cult classic we all know and love. 
Goat Sim - The most accurate simulator ever made they even use it to train goats into becoming professional goats

the jankiness, the weird bugs, the painfully bad controls in the waste of space dlc 
and the absurdness of the setting

packed full of references and satire humour there's something for everyone

from pro flappy bird players to bronies this game has it all

It's so good they skipped the sequel and went straight to the third game because we all know sequels are never as good as the originals (other than shrek 2)

And that is why you should play goat sim.

I got to be a goat, and almost crash out during flappy bird, I got to be an astronaut, and almost crash out due to spaceship control. 10/10 would baa again. (you do need all dlc for the achievements which is always slightly annoying but if they're on sale it's not that bad, they're all pretty fun too so knock yourself out)

claims.claim: Reviewers describe achievement hunting as tedious, requiring significant grind and a Steam friend for specific achievements.

citations.review_text:
[h1] Purchase Date: [/h1]
13th of January 2024 - 13/01/2024

[h1] Purchase Value: [/h1]
5.47€ ("Goat Simulator: GOATY" Bundle) 


[h1] PROS & CONS Review: [/h1]
PROS:
+ Classic.
+ Challenge variety.
+ Chaotic.
+ Easter eggs.

CONS:
- Repetitive after some time.
- Some amount of bugs.
- Hard to 100% Steam achievements.
- Some grinding needed to 100% Steam achievements.
- A Steam friend is required for 1 achievement.


[h1] Text Review: [/h1]
Goat Simulator is a title that probably every gamer has heard of at least once. It's a classic in the video game industry that made quite a bit of noise when it was first released, plaguing YouTube with a lot of new content to be seen.
It's simple, you're a naughty goat in a world where everything breaks, explodes and ultimately turns into total chaos.
Although the game is fun to play, it gets boring quickly.
There are quite a few bugs and sometimes crashes and it's easily understandable, with so much environment destruction, it's completely natural for the game to eventually crash. There even are achievements for this situation in particular. Some people might enjoy it, I didn't.
The challenge variety is very good, there's a lot to be done within the game.
It's also a great video game for people who enjoy discovering easter eggs without any instructions to do so.
This line is for the achievement hunters. It's hard and requires some grinding to 100% Steam achievements. Also, there's 1 achievement in which the player needs a Steam friend logged into the game. I recommend searching for the guide named "Goat Simulator - 100% Guide (2026 Up to date, BFF help)", it was this guide that mostly assisted me reaching 100% along with its author for the "BFF" achievement.


[h1] Recommendation: [/h1]
Overall, it was a good experience, although I think it's overrated.
I recommend it, buy it with a significant discount though.


[h1] Rating - 60/100 [/h1]
Review Date - 21/03/2026

Super nostalgic, still has that 2010s vibe. Personally didn't feel like it was optimized and had some lag but it may be my pc. Extremely tedious for trophy hunters if you're not a superfan of the game and actually enjoy the raw game for itself
